```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  warning = FALSE,

  fig.width = 13,

  out.width = "100%"

```

**Language / Idioma:** [English](visualization.html) | [Português](visualization_pt.html)

This module consolidates prediction metrics, compares models through paired Pearson bootstrap, and presents manuscript tables and figures. Computation and exports are executed explicitly in the English version; both documents render the new results without refitting models or overwriting files.


## 1. Load packages and locate project folders

This step loads the packages used for table manipulation, figure construction, and HTML table formatting. The paths below assume that the document is rendered from the project root.

```{r packages-and-paths}
rm(list = ls())
options(scipen = 999)

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(readr)
library(tibble)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggthemes)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
library(stringr)
library(patchwork)
library(grid)

project_root <- getwd()
results_dir <- file.path(project_root, "output", "results")
figures_dir <- file.path(project_root, "output", "figures")
tables_dir <- file.path(project_root, "output", "tables")
individual_predictions_dir <- file.path(results_dir, "individual_predictions")
env_levels <- c("CS11_WS", "CS11_WW", "CS12_WS", "CS12_WW")

```

## 2. Model catalog used in the prediction summaries

The catalog defines the 18 models compared in the prediction study. The column `Model` gives the label used in manuscript tables and figures (`M1`--`M18`), whereas `EtaName` keeps the computational identifier used internally in file names and BGLR run folders (`Eta1`--`Eta18`).

The pairs below compare the same modeling pathway and kernel family with and without the weather kernel.

```{r comparison-pairs}

)
```

## 4. Prediction summary tables

### 4.1 Consolidation of fold-level results

The 18,000 metric CSVs and corresponding individual RDS files are identified from the expected paths in Part II. Execute these chunks explicitly in English after validating the new fits. The three metrics are calculated in Part II and consolidated here without weighting by the number of pairs or valid correlations.

For each environment, the mean and sample standard deviation are calculated directly from the 50 metrics (ten repetitions and five folds). The across-environment mean is the arithmetic mean of the four environment means, equivalent to the direct mean of all 200 values when complete. The across-environment SD describes dispersion of available individual metrics, including between environments. Valid counts are reported; an undefined environmental mean prevents a four-environment mean.

```{r rebuild-prediction-summaries, eval=FALSE}
# Expected file paths follow the design in Part I.
inventory_cv12 <- expand.grid(
  CV = c("CV1", "CV2"), Trait = c("GY", "KW"),
  Rep = sprintf("rep%02d", 1:10), Fold = sprintf("fold%02d", 1:5),
  EtaName = paste0("Eta", 1:18), stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

inventory_cv12$Model <- sub("Eta", "M", inventory_cv12$EtaName)
inventory_cv12$file_name <- with(inventory_cv12,
  paste0(CV, "_", Trait, "_", EtaName, "_", Rep, "_", Fold, ".csv"))
inventory_cv12$relative_path <- with(inventory_cv12,
  file.path(CV, Trait, Rep, Fold, file_name))

inventory_cvloo <- expand.grid(
  CV = c("CV0", "CV00"), Env_leave = c("CS11_WS", "CS11_WW", "CS12_WS", "CS12_WW"),
  Trait = c("GY", "KW"), Rep = sprintf("rep%02d", 1:10),
  Fold = sprintf("fold%02d", 1:5), EtaName = paste0("Eta", 1:18),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

inventory_cvloo$Model <- sub("Eta", "M", inventory_cvloo$EtaName)
inventory_cvloo$file_name <- with(inventory_cvloo,
  paste0(CV, "_", Trait, "_", Env_leave, "_", EtaName, "_", Rep, "_", Fold, ".csv"))
inventory_cvloo$relative_path <- with(inventory_cvloo,
  file.path(CV, Env_leave, Trait, Rep, Fold, file_name))

inventory_cv12 <- inventory_cv12[, c("relative_path", "file_name", "CV", "Trait",
                                      "Rep", "Fold", "EtaName", "Model")]
inventory_cvloo <- inventory_cvloo[, c("relative_path", "file_name", "CV", "Env_leave",
                                       "Trait", "Rep", "Fold", "EtaName", "Model")]

combined_inventory <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  inventory_cv12 %>% dplyr::mutate(Env_leave = NA_character_),
  inventory_cvloo
)

combined_inventory$individual_path <- file.path(
  "individual_predictions",
  sub("\\.csv$", ".rds", combined_inventory$relative_path)
)

combined_inventory$Metrics_available <- file.exists(
  file.path(results_dir, combined_inventory$relative_path)
)
combined_inventory$Individual_available <- file.exists(
  file.path(results_dir, combined_inventory$individual_path)
)

# The expected inventory is fixed by the validation design.
# Historical CSVs without the new metrics cannot enter the consolidation.
stopifnot(
  nrow(combined_inventory) == 18000L,
  all(combined_inventory$Metrics_available),
  all(combined_inventory$Individual_available),
  file.exists(file.path(results_dir, "fold_partitions.csv"))
)

metric_columns <- c("Env", "cor", "Spearman", "Czekanowski", "N",
                    "N_selected", "N_coincident", "Runtime_sec", "Fold")

metric_records <- vector("list", nrow(combined_inventory))

for (i in seq_len(nrow(combined_inventory))) {
  entry <- combined_inventory[i, ]
  x <- read.csv(file.path(results_dir, entry$relative_path),
                stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

  expected_env <- if (is.na(entry$Env_leave)) env_levels else entry$Env_leave

  stopifnot(
    identical(names(x), metric_columns),
    !anyDuplicated(x$Env),
    setequal(x$Env, expected_env),
    all(x$Fold == entry$Fold)
  )

  x$CV <- entry$CV
  x$Trait <- entry$Trait
  x$Rep <- as.integer(sub("rep", "", entry$Rep))
  x$Fold <- as.integer(sub("fold", "", entry$Fold))
  x$Model <- entry$EtaName
  x$ModelNumber <- as.integer(sub("Eta", "", entry$EtaName))
  x$Env_leave <- entry$Env_leave

  metric_records[[i]] <- x
}

prediction_raw <- dplyr::bind_rows(metric_records)

stopifnot(
  nrow(prediction_raw) == 28800L,
  !anyDuplicated(prediction_raw[, c("CV", "Trait", "Env", "Rep", "Fold", "Model")]),
  all(is.na(prediction_raw$cor) | abs(prediction_raw$cor) <= 1),
  all(is.na(prediction_raw$Spearman) | abs(prediction_raw$Spearman) <= 1),
  all(is.na(prediction_raw$Czekanowski) |
      (prediction_raw$Czekanowski >= 0 & prediction_raw$Czekanowski <= 1))
)

rm(metric_records)

cv12_raw <- prediction_raw %>%
  dplyr::filter(CV %in% c("CV1", "CV2")) %>%
  dplyr::select(-Env_leave)

cvloo_raw <- prediction_raw %>%
  dplyr::filter(CV %in% c("CV0", "CV00"))
```

```{r summarize-prediction-metrics, eval=FALSE}
# Keep the individual fold metrics as the descriptive units.
metrics_by_environment <- prediction_raw %>%
  dplyr::group_by(ModelNumber, Model, Trait, CV, Env) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    MeanCorrelation = mean(cor, na.rm = TRUE),
    SDCorrelation = sd(cor, na.rm = TRUE),
    MeanSpearman = mean(Spearman, na.rm = TRUE),
    SDSpearman = sd(Spearman, na.rm = TRUE),
    MeanCzekanowski = mean(Czekanowski, na.rm = TRUE),
    SDCzekanowski = sd(Czekanowski, na.rm = TRUE),
    N_Pearson = sum(is.finite(cor)),
    N_Spearman = sum(is.finite(Spearman)),
    N_Czekanowski = sum(is.finite(Czekanowski)),
    NumberOfRepetitions = dplyr::n_distinct(Rep[is.finite(cor)]),
    MeanRuntimeSec = mean(Runtime_sec, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(where(is.numeric), ~ replace(.x, is.nan(.x), NA_real_)))

# Equal environmental weights even when valid-fold counts differ.
across_means <- metrics_by_environment %>%
  dplyr::group_by(ModelNumber, Model, Trait, CV) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    MeanCorrelation = mean(MeanCorrelation),
    MeanSpearman = mean(MeanSpearman),
    MeanCzekanowski = mean(MeanCzekanowski),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

across_dispersion <- prediction_raw %>%
  dplyr::group_by(ModelNumber, Model, Trait, CV) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    SDCorrelation = sd(cor, na.rm = TRUE),
    SDSpearman = sd(Spearman, na.rm = TRUE),
    SDCzekanowski = sd(Czekanowski, na.rm = TRUE),
    N_Pearson = sum(is.finite(cor)),
    N_Spearman = sum(is.finite(Spearman)),
    N_Czekanowski = sum(is.finite(Czekanowski)),
    NumberOfRepetitions = dplyr::n_distinct(Rep[is.finite(cor)]),
    MeanRuntimeSec = mean(Runtime_sec, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

metrics_across_environments <- dplyr::left_join(
  across_means, across_dispersion, by = c("ModelNumber", "Model", "Trait", "CV")
)

cv12_summary_rebuilt <- metrics_across_environments %>%
  dplyr::filter(CV %in% c("CV1", "CV2")) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(Trait, CV, ModelNumber)

cvloo_summary_rebuilt <- metrics_by_environment %>%
  dplyr::filter(CV %in% c("CV0", "CV00")) %>%
  dplyr::rename(Env_leave = Env, NumberOfRuns = NumberOfRepetitions) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(Trait, CV, Env_leave, ModelNumber)

# Retain the intermediate tables for inspection, not as inputs to the SD.
cv12_env_fold <- cv12_raw %>%
  dplyr::mutate(EnvCorrelation = cor, ValidationCount = as.integer(is.finite(cor)),
                MeanRuntimeSec = Runtime_sec)

cvloo_env_fold <- cvloo_raw %>%
  dplyr::mutate(LOEOCorrelation = cor, ValidationCount = as.integer(is.finite(cor)),
                MeanRuntimeSec = Runtime_sec)

cv12_env_rep <- cv12_env_fold %>%
  dplyr::group_by(ModelNumber, Model, Trait, CV, Rep, Env) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    EnvCorrelation = mean(cor, na.rm = TRUE),
    Spearman = mean(Spearman, na.rm = TRUE),
    Czekanowski = mean(Czekanowski, na.rm = TRUE),
    ValidationCount = sum(ValidationCount),
    MeanRuntimeSec = mean(Runtime_sec, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

cvloo_rep_summary <- cvloo_env_fold %>%
  dplyr::group_by(ModelNumber, Model, Trait, CV, Env_leave, Rep) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    LOEOCorrelation = mean(cor, na.rm = TRUE),
    Spearman = mean(Spearman, na.rm = TRUE),
    Czekanowski = mean(Czekanowski, na.rm = TRUE),
    ValidationCount = sum(ValidationCount),
    MeanRuntimeSec = mean(Runtime_sec, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

stopifnot(nrow(metrics_by_environment) == 576L,
          nrow(metrics_across_environments) == 144L,
          nrow(cv12_summary_rebuilt) == 72L,
          nrow(cvloo_summary_rebuilt) == 288L)
```

#### Paired Pearson comparisons

Inference is restricted to Pearson. Each resample draws ten repetitions with replacement, keeping the five folds, relevant environments and all 18 models paired. Repetition means are only a computationally equivalent way of computing bootstrap means of complete metrics. For all 153 contrasts in each trait × scenario × environment (or four-environment mean) family, we calculate the centered error of each difference and the 95th percentile of the maximum absolute error. The approximate simultaneous interval is the observed difference plus or minus this quantile. Incomplete families are identified and receive no inference; undefined correlations are never replaced with zero. Resampling does not quantify uncertainty for a new genotype population; with ten blocks, coverage is approximate and conditional on existing data and fits. Spearman and Czekanowski remain descriptive.

```{r paired-pearson-bootstrap, eval=FALSE}
n_boot <- 5000L
bootstrap_seed <- 20261125L
confidence_level <- 0.95
model_names <- paste0("M", 1:18)
model_pairs <- combn(model_names, 2L)

set.seed(bootstrap_seed)

# Each row contains the frequency of each of the ten sampled repetitions.
# Use identical draws for all 18 models and all evaluation families.
bootstrap_weights <- t(replicate(
  n_boot, tabulate(sample.int(10L, 10L, replace = TRUE), nbins = 10L)
)) / 10

bootstrap_families <- expand.grid(
  Trait = c("GY", "KW"),
  CV = c("CV1", "CV2", "CV0", "CV00"),
  Scope = c(env_levels, "Across"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

bootstrap_results <- vector("list", nrow(bootstrap_families))

for (g in seq_len(nrow(bootstrap_families))) {
  family <- bootstrap_families[g, ]
  records <- prediction_raw %>%
    dplyr::filter(Trait == family$Trait, CV == family$CV)

  target_env <- if (family$Scope == "Across") env_levels else family$Scope
  records <- records %>% dplyr::filter(Env %in% target_env)

  # Complete paired families only. Missing correlations are never zero.
  expected_n <- 18L * 10L * 5L * length(target_env)
  complete_family <- nrow(records) == expected_n && all(is.finite(records$cor))

  result <- data.frame(
    Trait = family$Trait, CV = family$CV, Scope = family$Scope,
    ModelA = model_pairs[1, ], ModelB = model_pairs[2, ],
    MeanA = NA_real_, MeanB = NA_real_, Difference = NA_real_,
    Lower95 = NA_real_, Upper95 = NA_real_, Significant = NA,
    SimultaneousHalfWidth = NA_real_, B = n_boot,
    N_Repetitions = if (complete_family) 10L else NA_integer_, N_ValidMetrics = sum(is.finite(records$cor)),
    Status = if (complete_family) "Complete" else "Undefined Pearson metric",
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  # Descriptive means remain available even if a family cannot be tested.
  descriptive <- if (family$Scope == "Across") metrics_across_environments else
    metrics_by_environment[metrics_by_environment$Env == family$Scope, ]
  descriptive <- descriptive[descriptive$Trait == family$Trait &
                               descriptive$CV == family$CV, ]
  descriptive_means <- setNames(descriptive$MeanCorrelation,
                                sub("Eta", "M", descriptive$Model))
  result$MeanA <- unname(descriptive_means[result$ModelA])
  result$MeanB <- unname(descriptive_means[result$ModelB])
  result$Difference <- result$MeanB - result$MeanA

  if (complete_family) {
    repetition_means <- records %>%
      dplyr::mutate(Model = sub("Eta", "M", Model)) %>%
      dplyr::group_by(Rep, Model) %>%
      dplyr::summarise(Score = mean(cor), .groups = "drop") %>%
      tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Model, values_from = Score) %>%
      dplyr::arrange(Rep)

    score_matrix <- as.matrix(repetition_means[, model_names])
    observed_means <- colMeans(score_matrix)

    stopifnot(
      identical(dim(score_matrix), c(10L, 18L)),
      isTRUE(all.equal(unname(observed_means),
                       unname(descriptive_means[model_names]), tolerance = 1e-12))
    )

    boot_means <- bootstrap_weights %*% score_matrix

    mean_a <- observed_means[model_pairs[1, ]]
    mean_b <- observed_means[model_pairs[2, ]]
    observed_delta <- mean_b - mean_a
    bootstrap_delta <- boot_means[, model_pairs[2, ], drop = FALSE] -
      boot_means[, model_pairs[1, ], drop = FALSE]

    # Center each contrast on its observed estimate before taking the maximum.
    # The 95th percentile of the maximum absolute error gives one
    # simultaneous half-width for all 153 contrasts on the Pearson scale.
    centered <- sweep(bootstrap_delta, 2L, observed_delta, "-")
    max_error <- apply(abs(centered), 1L, max)
    half_width <- as.numeric(quantile(max_error, confidence_level, type = 1))

    result$MeanA <- unname(mean_a)
    result$MeanB <- unname(mean_b)
    result$Difference <- unname(observed_delta)
    result$Lower95 <- unname(observed_delta - half_width)
    result$Upper95 <- unname(observed_delta + half_width)
    result$Significant <- result$Lower95 > 0 | result$Upper95 < 0
    result$SimultaneousHalfWidth <- half_width

    stopifnot(
      all(result$Lower95 <= result$Difference),
      all(result$Upper95 >= result$Difference),
      mean(max_error <= half_width) >= confidence_level
    )
  }

  bootstrap_results[[g]] <- result
}

bootstrap_comparisons <- dplyr::bind_rows(bootstrap_results)

# Tag matched contrasts for discussion without limiting the comparisons.
scientific_pairs <- data.frame(
  ModelA = paste0("M", c(1,3,5,2,4,6,7,8,9,
                         1,1,2,2,7,7,10,10,11,11,12,12,
                         1,2,3,4,5,6,10,11,13,14,16,17)),
  ModelB = paste0("M", c(10,13,16,11,14,17,12,15,18,
                         3,5,4,6,8,9,13,16,14,17,15,18,
                         7,7,8,8,9,9,12,12,15,15,18,18)),
  ScientificContrast = rep(c("Weather", "Kernel", "Integration"), c(9,12,12)),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

bootstrap_comparisons <- bootstrap_comparisons %>%
  dplyr::left_join(scientific_pairs, by = c("ModelA", "ModelB")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(ScientificContrast = tidyr::replace_na(ScientificContrast, "Other"))

stopifnot(nrow(bootstrap_comparisons) == 6120L,
          sum(bootstrap_comparisons$ScientificContrast != "Other") == 1320L,
          !anyDuplicated(bootstrap_comparisons[, c("Trait", "CV", "Scope", "ModelA", "ModelB")]))
```

Exports are executed once in the English version.

```{r export-prediction-summaries, eval=FALSE}
dir.create(tables_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

readr::write_csv(cv12_raw, file.path(tables_dir, "prediction_cv1_cv2_raw.csv"))
readr::write_csv(cvloo_raw, file.path(tables_dir, "prediction_cv0_cv00_raw.csv"))
readr::write_csv(cv12_env_fold, file.path(tables_dir, "prediction_cv1_cv2_by_rep_fold_env.csv"))
readr::write_csv(cvloo_env_fold, file.path(tables_dir, "prediction_cv0_cv00_by_rep_fold_env.csv"))
readr::write_csv(cv12_env_rep, file.path(tables_dir, "prediction_cv1_cv2_by_rep_env.csv"))
readr::write_csv(cvloo_rep_summary, file.path(tables_dir, "prediction_cv0_cv00_by_run.csv"))
readr::write_csv(cv12_summary_rebuilt, file.path(tables_dir, "prediction_cv1_cv2_summary.csv"))
readr::write_csv(cvloo_summary_rebuilt, file.path(tables_dir, "prediction_cv0_cv00_summary.csv"))
readr::write_csv(metrics_by_environment, file.path(tables_dir, "prediction_metrics_by_environment.csv"))
readr::write_csv(metrics_across_environments, file.path(tables_dir, "prediction_metrics_across_environments.csv"))

readr::write_csv(
```

### 8.1 Complementary metrics and supplementary comparisons

The complete metric table includes the four environments and across-environment mean, with valid counts. Pearson comparisons are exported in two CSVs, one per trait, with 3,060 rows each. Positive differences favor model B; simultaneous intervals excluding zero indicate detectable differences at the family level. Scientific contrasts guide discussion. No inferential comparisons are performed for Spearman or Czekanowski.


### 8.2 Global genotype rankings

Load all individual predictions. For ranking only, average each observation's predictions within repetition, then average the ten repetitions. Rankings are constructed separately by trait, scenario, environment and model; ties are resolved by Pedigree, and selection uses the top 20%, rounded up. These results do not replace fold metrics. CV2 is an in-sample evaluation.

```{r load-individual-predictions}
individual_files <- sort(list.files(
  individual_predictions_dir, pattern = "\\.rds$", recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE
))

stopifnot(length(individual_files) == 18000L)

individual_predictions <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(individual_files, readRDS))

stopifnot(
  nrow(individual_predictions) == 3535200L,
  all(c("ObsID", "Pedigree", "Env", "Trait", "Model", "Rep", "Fold",
        "Env_leave", "Observed", "Predicted", "Training", "CV") %in%
      names(individual_predictions)),
  !anyDuplicated(individual_predictions[, c("ObsID", "Trait", "Model", "Rep", "Fold", "CV")]),
  all(is.finite(individual_predictions$Observed)),
  all(is.finite(individual_predictions$Predicted))
)
```

```{r rank-genotypes, eval=FALSE}
# Retain all observations for the plots. Average only for global rankings.
ranking_by_rep <- individual_predictions %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Trait, CV, Env, Model, ObsID, Pedigree, Rep) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    Observed = dplyr::first(Observed),
    Predicted = mean(Predicted),
    N_Predictions = dplyr::n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

genotype_ranking <- ranking_by_rep %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Trait, CV, Env, Model, ObsID, Pedigree) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    Observed = dplyr::first(Observed),
    MeanPredicted = mean(Predicted),
    N_Repetitions = dplyr::n_distinct(Rep),
    N_Predictions = sum(N_Predictions),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Trait, CV, Env, Model) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(desc(Observed), Pedigree, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(ObservedRank = dplyr::row_number()) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(desc(MeanPredicted), Pedigree, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    PredictedRank = dplyr::row_number(),
    N_Selected = ceiling(0.20 * dplyr::n()),
    ObservedSelected = ObservedRank <= N_Selected,
    PredictedSelected = PredictedRank <= N_Selected
  ) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()

stopifnot(nrow(genotype_ranking) == 141408L,
          all(genotype_ranking$N_Repetitions == 10L),
          all(genotype_ranking$N_Predictions ==
                ifelse(genotype_ranking$CV %in% c("CV1", "CV00"), 10L, 40L)))
```

```{r export-genotype-ranking, eval=FALSE}
readr::write_csv(genotype_ranking, file.path(tables_dir, "prediction_genotype_ranking.csv"))
```

## 9. Figures

The original Pearson figures retain the M1–M18 catalog and presentation style. Bars are arithmetic means; error bars are standard deviations of individual fold metrics, not standard errors or confidence intervals. CV1/CV2 summaries include four environments; CV0/CV00 keep the held-out environment fixed within each panel. Fold genotype membership varies across repetitions, in addition to MCMC variability. CV2 represents in-sample recovery.

```{r figure-cv12}
group_levels_en <- c("Genomic", "Phenomic", "Combined")
model_levels_en <- model_catalog$Model

cv12_plot_data <- cv12_summary %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Group = factor(Group, levels = group_levels_en),
    Model = factor(Model, levels = model_levels_en),
    CV = factor(CV, levels = c("CV1", "CV2"))
  )

plot_gy <- cv12_plot_data %>%
  dplyr::filter(Trait == "GY") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Model, y = MeanCorrelation, fill = Group)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.75, color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.25, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(MeanCorrelation,3)), position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), angle = 90) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = MeanCorrelation - SDCorrelation, ymax = MeanCorrelation + SDCorrelation), width = 0.20, linewidth = 0.35, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.35) +
```

### 9.1 Spearman and Czekanowski

The supplementary figures are descriptive and present means and standard deviations of fold-level values.

```{r figure-complementary-metrics}
complementary_plot_data <- metric_summary %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(MeanSpearman, SDSpearman, MeanCzekanowski, SDCzekanowski),
    names_to = c(".value", "Metric"), names_pattern = "(Mean|SD)(.*)"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Model = factor(Model, levels = model_catalog$Model),
                Scope = factor(Scope, levels = c(env_levels, "Across")))

complementary_plots <- list()

for (trait in c("GY", "KW")) {
  for (cv in c("CV1", "CV2", "CV0", "CV00")) {
    for (metric in c("Spearman", "Czekanowski")) {
      plot_data <- complementary_plot_data %>%
        dplyr::filter(Trait == trait, CV == cv, Metric == metric)

      plot_name <- paste(trait, cv, metric, sep = "_")

      complementary_plots[[plot_name]] <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(Model, Mean, fill = Metric)) +
        geom_col(width = 0.75, color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.25) +
        geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = Mean - SD, ymax = Mean + SD), width = 0.2) +
        facet_wrap(~ Scope, ncol = 2) +
  ggthemes::scale_fill_gdocs(guide = "none") +
        labs(title = paste(trait, cv, metric, sep = " | "),
             x = "Model", y = "Mean metric") +
        theme_bw(base_size = 13)

      print(complementary_plots[[plot_name]])
    }
  }
}
```

### 9.2 Observed versus predicted values

Each figure includes all 18 models for one trait, scenario and environment. All points are retained without averaging by observation; the same observations appear in multiple folds or repetitions and are not independent. The dashed line indicates identity. CV2 is in-sample recovery.

```{r figure-observed-predicted, fig.width=16, fig.height=10}
observed_predicted_plots <- list()

for (trait in c("GY", "KW")) {
  for (cv in c("CV1", "CV2", "CV0", "CV00")) {
    for (env in env_levels) {
      plot_data <- individual_predictions %>%
        dplyr::filter(Trait == trait, CV == cv, Env == env) %>%
        dplyr::mutate(Model = factor(Model, levels = model_catalog$Model))

      plot_name <- paste(trait, cv, env, sep = "_")

      observed_predicted_plots[[plot_name]] <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(Observed, Predicted)) +
        geom_point(alpha = 0.18, size = 0.6, color = ggthemes::gdocs_pal()(3)[1]) +
        geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
        facet_wrap(~ Model, ncol = 6) +
        coord_equal() +
        labs(title = paste(trait, cv, env, sep = " | "),
             x = "Observed", y = "Predicted") +
        theme_bw(base_size = 12)

      print(observed_predicted_plots[[plot_name]])
    }
  }
}
```

TIFF exports are executed explicitly in the English version only.

```{r export-supplementary-figures, eval=FALSE}
dir.create(figures_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

for (plot_name in names(complementary_plots)) {
  ggsave(file.path(figures_dir, paste0("prediction_", plot_name, ".tiff")),
         plot = complementary_plots[[plot_name]], width = 16, height = 10,
         dpi = 300, compression = "lzw", bg = "white")
}

for (plot_name in names(observed_predicted_plots)) {
  ggsave(file.path(figures_dir, paste0("prediction_observed_predicted_", plot_name, ".tiff")),
         plot = observed_predicted_plots[[plot_name]], width = 16, height = 10,
         dpi = 300, compression = "lzw", bg = "white")
}
```

## 10. Final note

This module retains the original ten sections and presents descriptive results and Pearson comparisons. Model differences are reported in supplementary tables, not contrast figures. Rendering reads the new results and neither refits models nor exports files.
